rows.en: <library(1)><operator(30030,1)><speed(2)>Let me tell you what was learned from talking with Capt. <color(4)>Jamil<ce()>. To start with the conclusion: this is Earth.
<operator(30030,1)><speed(2)>The year and the date matched<thumbnail(172)>, and the surrounding celestial bodies are those of Earth itself.
<operator(30030,1)><speed(2)>Hard as it is to believe, all that can be said is that this is "somewhere else", different from the Earth<thumbnail(173)> we live on.
<operator(30030,1)><speed(2)>To be honest, I am bewildered too... but right now, grasping the situation comes first.
<thumbdown()><operator(30030,1)><speed(2)>For the time being, while cooperating with Capt. <color(4)>Jamil<ce()>, we will gather information and look into a way to return.
<library(2)><topic()><operator(30080,1)><speed(2)>Your ship... Should we really call it the <color(4)>Nadesico<ce()>? It is a rather unusual name...
<operator(30080,1)><speed(2)>Well, never mind. There is something I should tell you.

<operator(30080,1)><speed(2)>This was learned by intercepting <book(38)>New Federation<endbook()> communications: it seems the <book(38)>New Federation<endbook()> had already<thumbnail(174)> marked you.
rows.notes: Active voice so both book spans precede the thumbnail as in source.

rows.en: <operator(30080,1)><speed(2)>If your story of having come from another world is true, it is extremely unnatural for word to get around this fast.
<thumbdown()><operator(30080,1)><speed(2)>There may be someone in the <book(38)>New Federation<endbook()> who knows of you. Let us stay careful about information.

uncertainties.issue: Archive titles "History of the Other World" / "The Nadesico's Situation": descriptive; width limit of the archive list unknown to me. Glossary note warns that "the other world" is viewpoint-dependent; here the viewpoint is the Nadesico crew's, so it means the world they arrived in.
"nengou ya hizuke wa icchi" - matched (with ours); "shuuhen no tentai no joukyou mo chikyuu sono mono" -> surrounding celestial bodies are those of Earth itself.
"jouhou ni wa chuui wo haratte okimashou" - either "be careful with (our) information" or "pay attention to intel"; kept open with "stay careful about information".

checked_decisions: Slots 0 and 1 are BOTH archive topic titles: <library(1)> (slot 19) opens topic 1 and <library(2)> (slot 24) opens topic 2. Neighbouring archives show the same layout (4003972 has three title slots 0-2; 4003982 and 4003992 have two). Both rows are translated and both are correct: slot 0 "isekai no rekishi" -> "History of the Other World", slot 1 "Nadeshiko no joukyou" -> "The Nadesico's Situation".
Slot 0 ruling: the glossary warns against mapping "the other world" to Earth A/B; the draft does not map it, so the warning is respected.
Slot 20 ruling: "matched" (with the Nadesico's own calendar) and "celestial bodies are those of Earth itself" are correct.
Slot 28 ruling: the source is ambiguous between guarding one's own information and watching incoming intel; "stay careful about information" keeps both, accepted.
"Capt. Jamil" follows the orchestrator decision for kanchou. Slot 26: active voice keeps both book spans before <thumbnail(174)> as in the source; meaning unchanged.
Slots 20, 21: <thumbnail> follows the same word as in the source.
remaining_uncertainties: Slot 0: the topic text (slots 19-23) is about the Nadesico crew finding out this is a different Earth, not really "history"; the title is translated literally as the source has it.
Slot 24: "Should we really call it" supplies "we" (source has no subject; Sala could mean "I"). Left as harmless.
Slot 19: "from talking with Capt. Jamil" - literally "from Capt. Jamil's account"; same information, left.
Slot 21: "yahari" (after all) not rendered; no information lost, left.
Slots 0-1: visible width limit for archive list titles is not known (26 and 24 characters used).
